Pumpenai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžio apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Before Jews settled in Pumpenai, a Karaite community existed in the village; Rabbinic Jews arrived in the mid-18th century and eventually became the majority. A fire in 1861 destroyed most of the town's houses and its synagogue, killing seven Jews; a renovated bathhouse from the community's 1881 rebuilding still stands today. Pumpenai served as a center for Torah study, producing Rabbi Yehonathan Eliashberg (1850–1899), among the first rabbis of his generation to publish in newspapers and a committed Hovevei Zion activist, and Rabbi Hayim HaLevi Katz (1854–1932), a noted orator and prolific author on Jewish subjects. On August 26, 1941, Pumpenai's Jews were led to the Pajuoste forest near Panevėžys, documented elsewhere in this collection, and shot beside long pits; other families were taken to Pasvalys and then the Zadeikiai forest, also documented elsewhere. This cemetery's prewar stone fence was partly demolished during the Soviet era when a 1970 highway to Riga was built directly through the site.
